ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a container, with many identical gray circular particles inside; the particles are dispersed throughout the container; an arrow points to the container on the right. In the container on the right there are still gray circular particles of the same appearance, but they are tightly gathered at the bottom of the container. Reasoning: Comparing before and after the change, the symbols and types of the particles have not changed, no new particle type appears, and it does not show particles recombining into a new compound; what changes is only the positions and arrangement of the particles. Therefore the composition of the substance remains unchanged, which conforms to a physical change, not a chemical change.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram below models a change that occurs in matter. Based on what you know about changes in matter, explain why the diagram shows a physical change rather than a chemical change.
raw_record.standard_answer: The composition of the matter stays the same.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identical particles are dispersed in the initial container and then gathered closely at the bottom in the final container. Compare the particle symbols on both sides: since they remain the same kind of particle and are not rearranged into new types of particles or compounds, infer that the matter’s composition has not changed. Conclude that the diagram represents a physical change, not a chemical change.

method.model_answer: The diagram shows a physical change because the particles are still the same kind of particles before and after the change. Only their arrangement or spacing changes, so the composition of the matter stays the same.
